annotations.description: Played Hallowed Fountain paying 2 life when Island would have provided the same U mana untapped for free. The 2 life was wasted since Island enables Spell Snare equally well on turn 1, and future turns work out the same (Floodfarm Verge activates off Island too).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Hallowed Fountain, paying 2 life to enter untapped for U mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island for free untapped U mana, saving Hallowed Fountain for a later turn when the dual typing or W mana might matter more.

annotations.description: With 3 mana available (Forest, Ba Sing Se, Llanowar Elves), the player could cast Badgermole Cub (1G) which is a 2/2 that also earthbends a land into a creature with a +1/+1 counter, creating significantly more board presence. Instead they cast a second Llanowar Elves, which only adds a 1/1 body and mana acceleration. While ramping toward Mightform Harmonizer is reasonable, Badgermole Cub develops a much stronger board (2/2 + a 1/1 land creature) and the Cub's ability to generate extra mana from creature taps also provides acceleration. Additionally, playing into an opponent with Spell Snare mana open (UU available) is risky since Llanowar Elves costs 1 (not 2), but Badgermole Cub costs 2 and could be Spell Snared. However, they could also play Temple Garden first for an additional land, then have even more options. The sequencing of land drop before spell is also a consideration - they should play Temple Garden first regardless of which creature they cast.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Llanowar Elves (second copy) for G
annotations.betterLine: Play Temple Garden (paying 2 life or tapped), then cast Badgermole Cub for 1G, earthbending a land to create a stronger board presence. Alternatively, if wanting to play around Spell Snare on the 2-mana spell, casting Llanowar Elves is defensible but Temple Garden should still be played first.

annotations.description: Using No More Lies (a premium 2-mana counterspell) to counter a second Llanowar Elves when holding Day of Judgment to handle creatures and Spell Snare for 2-drops. No More Lies would be better saved for a high-impact spell like Mightform Harmonizer or another threat that Day of Judgment can't answer.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast No More Lies targeting the second Llanowar Elves, tapping both lands to pay WU.
annotations.betterLine: Let the Llanowar Elves resolve, play Sunbillow Verge next turn, and use Day of Judgment on turn 4 to sweep the board. Save No More Lies for a more impactful spell like Mightform Harmonizer.

annotations.description: The opponent has 3 untapped lands (Hallowed Fountain, Floodfarm Verge, Island) which is exactly enough mana to cast No More Lies (WU + 3 to pay is irrelevant - they can counter it). While No More Lies is already in the graveyard, the opponent could have other counterspells. More importantly, casting Mightform Harmonizer via Warp ({2}{G}) means it gets exiled at the next end step, making it a temporary threat. Meanwhile, the opponent likely has interaction ready with 3 open mana. Seam Rip (W) could have been cast first to exile a potential blocker or problematic permanent, and it's a permanent that sticks around. However, the bigger issue is that casting a Warp creature into open mana when the opponent is playing a UW control deck with counterspells is risky - if countered, you lose the card entirely (and with No More Lies-style effects, it gets exiled). The Warp version already exiles itself at end step, so the upside is just one combat step with landfall trigger doublings. Playing Seam Rip first (there are no valid targets with mana value 2 or less on opponent's board though - only lands) means Seam Rip actually has no valid targets here. So the real question is whether to cast Mightform Harmonizer via Warp into 3 open mana from a UW control opponent. Given the opponent already used No More Lies (it's in the graveyard), they might have Spell Snare (which hits MV 2, not MV 3 Warp cost). The risk is moderate but the line is reasonable to apply pressure. Actually, looking more carefully - the Warp cost is {2}{G} (MV 3), and the opponent has exactly the mana for counterspells like another No More Lies or similar. But the Harmonizer is being warped, meaning if it resolves, it provides a huge damage burst with landfall triggers doubling power. This is a tempo play that could be punished but also could be game-winning. This seems more questionable than a clear blunder.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mightform Harmonizer via Warp for {2}{G} into opponent's 3 open UW mana
annotations.betterLine: Consider holding Mightform Harmonizer and playing Ba Sing Se (land drop) first, then potentially waiting a turn to cast the full Harmonizer (non-Warp) when the opponent has to tap out, or baiting countermagic with a lesser spell first. Playing Ba Sing Se as the land drop this turn develops mana while keeping the Harmonizer for a more impactful non-Warp cast later.

annotations.description: Activating Ba Sing Se's earthbend 2 for 4 mana (3 mana + tap) when the opponent is completely tapped out leaves only 1 mana remaining, preventing deployment of the full hand. Deploying all three hand cards (Badgermole Cub + Sazh's Chocobo + Seam Rip for ~4 mana total) would put more bodies on board and still get earthbend 1 from Badgermole Cub's ETB trigger, maximizing the pressure window while the opponent can't interact.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Ba Sing Se's earthbend 2 ability for {2}{G}+{T}, consuming 4 of 5 available lands, leaving only 1 mana for remaining spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Badgermole Cub (1G) to get a 2/2 body + earthbend 1, then Sazh's Chocobo (G), then Seam Rip (W) to deploy the entire hand for 4 mana while the opponent is tapped out, maximizing board presence and pressure.

annotations.description: Failed to cast Sazh's Chocobo for {G} with one untapped Ba Sing Se available while opponent is completely tapped out. After a board wipe, deploying a creature with landfall synergy to start rebuilding is important, especially when the opponent can't interact.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without casting anything, leaving {G} mana unused and Sazh's Chocobo stranded in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sazh's Chocobo for {G} using the untapped Ba Sing Se. Opponent has all lands tapped and no way to counter or remove it this turn. The Chocobo would start growing with landfall triggers on subsequent turns.

annotations.description: The opponent has zero creatures on the battlefield — all their creatures are in exile. Day of Judgment would currently destroy nothing. Meanwhile, Jeskai Revelation is an extremely powerful card that bounces a permanent, deals 4 damage, creates tokens, draws 2 cards, and gains 4 life — all crucial when at 10 life needing to turn the corner with The Unagi of Kyoshi Island in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Day of Judgment and No More Lies from Consult the Star Charts.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Jeskai Revelation and No More Lies. Jeskai Revelation provides life gain, card advantage, removal, and board presence — far more impactful than a board wipe against an empty creature board. Deploy Unagi next turn with No More Lies backup, and have Jeskai Revelation as a powerful follow-up.

annotations.description: Playing Forest before casting Felidar Retreat means the landfall trigger from Forest won't trigger Felidar Retreat (since it's not on the battlefield yet). This wastes a landfall trigger that would have created a 2/2 Cat Beast token or pumped all creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest first (triggering only Sazh's Chocobo landfall), planning to cast Felidar Retreat afterward without a land drop remaining.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Felidar Retreat first (has 5 lands including Temple Garden for white mana, costing 3W), then play Forest to trigger both Felidar Retreat landfall (2/2 token or +1/+1 counters) and Sazh's Chocobo landfall.

annotations.description: At 7 opponent life with no blockers, casting Mightform Harmonizer with Warp ({2}{G}) would create a 4/4 hasty attacker dealing 4 damage (opponent to 3), putting them in lethal range next turn. Instead, earthbend 2 creates only a 2/2 attacker dealing 2 damage (opponent to 5), which is less pressure despite the creature persisting.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Ba Sing Se's earthbend 2 to create a 2/2 hasty land creature
annotations.betterLine: Cast Mightform Harmonizer with Warp for {2}{G} to get a 4/4 hasty attacker, dealing 4 damage and putting opponent to 3 life - within easy lethal range next turn

annotations.description: Grk41F Drama chose not to attack with Mightform Harmonizer (4/4) into an empty board when the opponent is at 7 life. Attacking would put the opponent to 3 life, making lethal trivially easy next turn. The opponent has no blockers, so there is zero risk in attacking.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Mightform Harmonizer, leaving the opponent comfortably at 7 life.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Mightform Harmonizer for 4 damage, putting the opponent to 3 life. This creates immediate lethal pressure and forces the opponent to find an answer or die next combat.
